not_modelled.what: Washington's excise tax on long-term capital gains (RCW 82.87), which is separate from income tax: 7% on the first 1,000,000 of taxable Washington capital gains and 7% plus an additional 2.9% on the amount over 1,000,000, after a 278,000 standard deduction and the record's other deductions and exemptions (real estate and assets held in certain retirement accounts are exempt). The projection computes none of it. Only a household whose Washington long-term gains exceed the standard deduction after exemptions can owe it; the warning fires only when the household has long-term gains.

derived_figures.what: Washington capital gains tax rate on the amount over 1,000,000: the 7% plus the additional 2.9%; matches the 9.9% row of the notice's rate table. Not used in any calculation here (the tax is in not_modelled).

approximations.what: No personal income tax (Income tax page, Washington Department of Revenue). Social Security and municipal interest are shown as exempt because nothing is taxed; the record holds not_stated for both, since the sources say nothing about either.
approximations.size: None: there is no state income tax to estimate.

approximations.what: Washington's tax on long-term capital gains is left out of the state tax (see not_modelled).
approximations.size: The whole tax, for a household that owes it. Example: 500,000 of Washington long-term gains after exemptions, no other deductions: (500,000 - 278,000) x 7% = 15,540 a year not shown.
